newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Intel stock stumbles.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Intel stock stumbles.

text.p: Intel Corp saw the largest waver from closing stock prices in after hours trading on Wednesday, trading down 1/2 at 147, dealers said.
Meanwhile, dealers had no after hours trades to report on News Corp Ltd despite the late-breaking news that International Family would merge with News Corp's Fox Kids Worldwide Inc unit.
International Family, owned by Christian evangelist Pat Robertson, remained halted as it announced that News Corp would pay $35.00 a share, in cash, in the merger deal.

News Corp, the media empire belonging to Rupert Murdoch, said Pat Robertson and his son Tim Robertson had agreed to sell their shares and that the latter would remain with International Family as president and chief executive officer.
The deal was valued at $1.9 billion, including the assumption of International Family's debt.
In regular hours trading, the Dow industrials rallied to their fourth consecutive record close, surging 37 points to an unofficial close of 7576.
The Nasdaq composite index also gained, rising more than six points, to almost 1408. Intel firmed to 147-1/2 during the day's trading, reflecting a recovery by technology stocks.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one volume rose Wednesday to 19,900 from 8,200 on Tuesday, while session two volume jumped to 11,366,416 from 260,000 the previous day.
